text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-eu-west GPU pool 'gpu-pool-eu-1' effective capacity falling: 98% token queue growth over last 3m, autoscaler attempted +12 nodes but 7 registrations failed; multiple nodes reporting CUDA Xid events and kernel oops. Paging oncall.

micah: oncall here, looking. which customers hit?

elaine: seeing qlen spike for /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints. throttling kicking in at 75th pct. top callers: marketplace-runner, analytics-batch.

yash: from runtime logs, several nodes show repeated "GPU Xid 79" messages and cuda driver resets. also OOMs on /dev/shm in a couple of pods. past 10m: 4 nodes flapped (Reconnect/NodeNotReady).

micah: can someone paste the dmesg/nvidia-smi output from a flapping node?

elaine: attaching excerpt:
```
[root@gpu-12 ~]# dmesg | tail -n 40
[123456.789] NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[123456.792] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed!
[123456.796] nvme0n1: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2345678
[123456.801] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (python) score 892 or sacrifice child
```
```
[root@gpu-12 ~]# nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS
GPU 0: Xid 79, Reset required
GPU 1: Xid 31, ECC errors
Temperature: 83 C
```

micah: ok Xid 79 + node level OOMs. sounds like driver/runtime instability reducing usable GPU count which prevents autoscaler from achieving desired capacity.

yash: also seeing this in runtime logs: "kvcache: failed to allocate GPU memory for batch 0 -> cudaErrorIllegalAddress" right before the Xid. probable memory corruption in driver or a bad kernel module.

archana: customer impact: several realtime apps seeing increased latency and 503s. early estimate: 4% of generation requests failing or retried, priority customers affected: analytics-batch (high), marketplace-runner (medium).

jess: I'll prepare a quick customer note draft: "We are investigating increased errors and throttling in EU region due to GPU node instability; we have mitigations in flight and will follow up in 30m." want to confirm affected customers before send.

micah: IC for this incident. immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop autoscaler from adding more nodes to this pool (avoid introducing more faulty hosts) 2) cordon/evacuate flapping nodes, restart driver on nodes that can recover 3) fail traffic to fallback pool in US if needed for high-tier customers 4) execute rolling restart for remaining nodes with driver reload or kernel reboot 5) postmortem & followups.

elaine: commands I'm running now:
```
# freeze autoscaler for pool
kubectl -n infra patch configmap gpu-autoscaler --type merge -p '{"data":{"enabled":"false"}}'
# cordon + drain known-flap nodes
kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# attempt remote driver restart
ssh root@gpu-12 'systemctl restart nvidia-driver || reboot'
```

micah: good. don't drain everything at once — leave capacity to keep serving. do one node at a time.

yash: adding: increase per-request token timeout and lower batch sizes on the runtime so memory pressure decreases. patching config now.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: runtime-config-update -> rollout started to 20% of pods in gpu-pool-eu-1.

micah: Elaine, track nodes that fail to re-register after restart. we'll mark them for full replace.

elaine: 2 nodes restarted and rejoined; 3 nodes failed to come up (still show NVRM Xid 79 in last 5m). marking those for replacement.

jess: drafting customer note and sending to legal/pg for review. ETA 10m.

archana: routing decision: for top-tier customers (SLA customers), route traffic to us-west fallback pool and mark their requests as high-priority to avoid retries. non-SLA customers will see degraded throughput until pool is healthy.

micah: make sure cost-control signals enabled on fallback (we don't want runaway spend). also enable model-level rate limiting to keep P99 latency stable.

yash: runtime config patch applied: batch_size=16 -> 8, request_timeout=60s -> 90s, prefix_cache_enabled=true. This should reduce memory spikes.

elaine: autoscaler remains disabled. opening a manual scale request to create replacement nodes in a different AZ: infra-provisioner creating replacements now.

deploy-bot: infra-provisioner: new nodes requested: 5 (type: a10g-like) in eu-west-2b.

micah: customer-suc, send initial message: jess please include a PS that we're working on failover and will share ETA for restoration.

jess: sent to affected contacts: "We've identified driver instability in EU causing increased errors. We have failed over top-tier traffic to fallback pool and are replacing unstable hosts. We'll update within 30 minutes or earlier."

archana: monitoring: queue length stabilized after redirect of priority traffic but total queued tokens still higher than normal. throttling reduced error-rate from 4% -> 1.2%.

yash: note for followup: capture full kernel traces from failed nodes and collect dmesg + core dumps. escalate driver to vendor with Xid 79 pattern and memory corruption hypothesis.

micah: agree. assign to oncall postmortem: collect core dumps, list of nodes, kernel versions, driver versions, and container images. Also schedule a firmware/driver bump window for non-peak hours.

elaine: replacing 3 failed nodes completed, new nodes healthy and registered. autoscaler still disabled until we confirm stability + driver patch verification.

micah: final immediate status: pool capacity back to 92% effective (not fully), queue growth reduced, autoscaler disabled, priority customers failed over, driver-restart + node replacement done. Incident remains open.

jess: customer update sent with current mitigation + ETA: 45m for full restore.

archana: opening incident doc (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/INC-2765432188) with timeline and impact.

micah: handing off to Elaine and Yash for long-term fix and postmortem. I'll update the oncall rotation. thanks all. :thumbsup:

elaine: on it. collecting artifacts now. will update the doc with logs + mitigation steps.

yash: working driver vendor ticket and scheduling driver/kernel upgrade.

incident-bot: NOTE: this thread was escalated to incident review. Add any extra context or reactions.

micah: closing the paging loop for now — if we see a new Xid wave, re-pager.

jess: will keep customers posted and loop in AM for follow-up postmortem notes.

-- end thread --
